Q: bash script error converting zip file to tar.gz (or tar.bz2) A:

Try this script (named zip-to-tar, tested on Ubuntu):

#!/bin/bash
dir=$(mktemp -d) file=$(realpath $2)
unzip "$1" -d "$dir" && tar zcf "$file" -C "$dir" .
rm -rf "$dir"
# example : zip-to-tar test.zip /tmp/test.tgz

Q: Kendo grid filter producing an `.addBack() is not a function` A:

addBack was added in jQuery 1.8, make sure you are on this version or more.

Q: How can I safely generate deterministic cache keys for complex PHP arrays (including objects) without risking collisions? A:

@KIKO Thanks for the insight. You're right that in some cases array order is semantically meaningful and should be preserved. In my situation the arrays mainly represent filter parameters and request inputs, where the order doesn't carry meaning (e.g., query parameters in a request), so I’m trying to normalize them to avoid generating multiple cache entries for logically identical inputs.

Good point regarding MD5 as well. I'm mostly using it here as a quick example for hashing the normalized structure rather than for cryptographic purposes, but I’ll review other algorithms like xxh3, sha256, etc. depending on the performance/collision trade-offs.

Out of curiosity, in your implementation do you simply hash the serialized input (e.g. serialize() / json_encode()), or do you use another approach for generating cache keys?

Q: MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE not working on Android TV? A:

Since there is no answer for a month, I will answer my question.

After testing on multiple versions of Android TV in emulator, I found that MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is only available in Android TV 13 to 16, not in Android TV 11 and 12.

Q: Debug Core dump in QNX - How to get more info? A:

My previously working code crashes now. The core dump points to the constructor being called. I have tried to get bt, bt full and disassembly. I need some help to conclude what could cause segmentation fault while calling constructor? Code is run on QNX and there is console gdb only. The local variables are all 0, what could that mean ?. I need some help to conclude what could cause segmentation fault while calling constructor?

Please do not conclude that there could be problem(only) while calling constructor. This can be just the side effect of something else(bad) which has already occurred. It would be difficult to figure out the problem from the current stack trace. Sometime memory bugs would be in very intermittent(due to different input/threading/change in sequence of execution),and program may run for years without showing any symptoms of any problem. The locals variables 0 may indicate that it looks ok but we can not conclude anything from it.

I do feel that there could be some memory corruption scenario (somewhere else in your other module)is leading this crash. You would have to debug your code using GDB/Valgrind(some dynamic tool) to find out the root problem. It looks like you are experiencing this problem on QNX, so you may want to run the Valgrind to identify the problem in your code. You can refer to my previous post

https://stackoverflow.com/a/22658693/2724703
